title: Gideon and the Locker
premise: Juniper Okonkwo has spent five years perfecting the art of staying out of trouble since her brother Gideon's death, but a forced semester project with her nemesis, Theo Vance, drags her into the town's fading tradition of the Locker — a century-old time capsule ceremony her brother once loved. As they restore the Locker for its final audition before the council scraps it, Juniper discovers Gideon's own contribution still sealed inside, along with letters revealing he knew he was sick and chose the tradition to leave her something. When Theo's family — the ones whose negligence case nearly destroyed hers — turns out to hold the deciding vote, Juniper must choose between winning the argument and honoring what her brother actually left behind. In the end she speaks not to win but to tell the truth, saving the Locker in altered form and finding that found family, including an unlikely friendship with Theo, is the real inheritance.
about_author: Petra Eastwick is a former high school debate coach who spent a decade watching teenagers say true things in the safest possible words. She writes from a converted garage in Ohio, where she keeps her own childhood locker door as a bookshelf.

chapters.title: The Art of Being Careful
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Five years after Gideon's death, Juniper wins the regional debate final while carefully avoiding every conversation about him at home. Her mother's silence and her father's long shifts have made the house a place of managed quiet. Emotional beat: competence as armor, loneliness beneath it.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Mr. Okafor pairs her with Theo Vance for the semester civics project: document and save one local tradition. Theo is the younger brother of the driver in the accident that killed Gideon. The classroom goes silent. Emotional beat: fury and dread colliding with no legal way out.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They negotiate ground rules at the library like hostile diplomats: no families, no past, no pity. Theo proposes the Locker, the town's 100-year-old time capsule ceremony facing a council vote. Emotional beat: wary truce built on mutual stubbornness.

chapters.title: What the Locker Was
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the rusted Locker behind the old middle school, Theo reveals his grandmother was its last keeper, and that his family's guilt over the accident runs deeper than Juniper knows. He doesn't explain; he just shows her the keeper's ledger. Emotional beat: first crack in the nemesis narrative.

chapters.title: Council Notice
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The town council announces the Locker site will be demolished for a parking expansion unless a 'viable stewardship plan' passes final audition in ten weeks. Juniper realizes the project just became a real fight. Emotional beat: reluctant investment turning into purpose.

chapters.title: Ledger of Small Things
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They interview elders who contributed to the Locker across decades — a retired mail carrier, the diner owner, Juniper's own fourth-grade teacher. Each story is a piece of the town's memory. Emotional beat: wonder; history becoming personal.

chapters.title: Home Game
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper's mother finds the ledger on the kitchen table and goes cold — it contains a photo of Gideon at age nine, adding his first item. Dinner detonates into the argument Juniper has avoided for five years. Emotional beat: the cost of memory at home.

chapters.title: The Other Brother
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confesses that his older brother Marcus wasn't driving that night — their father was — and Marcus took the blame and then left town. Theo has carried the secret alone. Emotional beat: guilt revealed as inheritance too.

chapters.title: Sealed Section
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Researching the Locker's bylaws, they discover a sealed contributor section opened only when the Locker faces closure — meaning Gideon's items may include private letters. Juniper can't decide if she wants them. Emotional beat: hope as a frightening thing.

chapters.title: Allies and Antagonists
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They recruit a ragtag committee: Mr. Okafor, the diner owner, two freshmen, and unexpectedly Marcus Vance, back in town for their father's trial. Old grudges flare at the first meeting. Emotional beat: found family assembling out of friction.

chapters.title: Debate Practice
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper trains the committee to present at the audition, but her coaching turns harsh and controlling — she's recreating the perfectionism that keeps her safe. Theo calls her out publicly. Emotional beat: seeing her own armor from outside.

chapters.title: Trial Days
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Marcus testifies; the truth about the accident becomes public, and Juniper's mother learns the Vance family hid it for five years. Juniper watches Theo's family fracture in parallel to her own. Emotional beat: grief recognizing grief.

chapters.title: The Apology That Isn't Enough
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Theo formally apologizes to Juniper's mother, who refuses it — not cruelly, but completely. Juniper defends him, splitting her loyalty down the middle. Emotional beat: forgiveness cannot be scheduled or owed.

chapters.title: Midnight at the Locker
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Unable to sleep before the hearing, Juniper visits the Locker alone and finds Theo there, doing the same. They talk without strategy for the first time — about Gideon, about Marcus, about being the siblings left behind. Emotional beat: intimacy through shared damage.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A developer's ally leaks that the 'stewardship plan' is a school project, mocking it in the press; two committee members quit, and the council chair moves the audition up two weeks. Emotional beat: the cause under real threat.

chapters.title: What Gideon Left
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. With closure imminent, the sealed section opens early by emergency petition. Inside: Gideon's letters, written during his illness, asking the keepers to give his sister 'an argument worth winning.' Juniper reads them in the empty gym. Emotional beat: devastating, loving inheritance.

chapters.title: The Argument at Home
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper finally brings the fight home — reads Gideon's letter aloud to her mother, who breaks her five-year silence and admits she couldn't bear the Locker because Gideon loved it more than anything. First honest tears. Emotional beat: grief unsealed.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Case
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The remaining committee rebuilds the presentation around testimony instead of polish: the elders, the letters, the kids who'll inherit the next century of items. Marcus agrees to speak. Emotional beat: fragile unity, real stakes.

chapters.title: Final Audition
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Before the council, opponents argue economics; Juniper abandons her prepared rebuttal and tells the truth — about Gideon, about Theo, about what towns lose when they pave over memory. She doesn't try to win. She tries to be believed. Emotional beat: climax; truth over victory.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Deadlocked, the council chair — Gideon's old debate coach — casts the deciding vote to preserve the Locker as a living archive run by students. The room erupts; Juniper and Theo stand together, stunned. Emotional beat: triumph earned, not argued.

chapters.title: New Items
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Spring reopening: the town contributes new objects; Juniper adds Gideon's debate medal, Theo adds Marcus's old locker key, and Juniper's mother adds a photo of all four kids. Families that were enemies share a table. Emotional beat: healing made ritual.

chapters.title: What You Keep
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Epilogue at summer's end: Juniper wins the state debate final and dedicates it to 'the people who taught me losing arguments can still mean everything.' She and Theo seal the year's items together. Emotional beat: inheritance accepted; carefulness released.
